name: Miami
summary: A subtropical, majority-Hispanic metro on Biscayne Bay, known for its beaches, Cuban and Caribbean food, Art Deco Miami Beach, nightlife and a fast-growing finance scene.

curated-2026-10.title: Miami places and neighborhoods written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge, covering the City of Miami plus Miami Beach and nearby municipalities people treat as neighborhoods (Coral Gables, Key Biscayne, Doral, Aventura, Miami Gardens). Businesses open and close and rents move: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical asking ranges, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighborhood centers.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for Miami (Miami International Airport area)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with NOAA 1991-2020 normals; refresh with scripts/world when network access to NOAA is available. The wet season runs May to October and the Atlantic hurricane season June to November.

neighborhoods.name: Brickell
neighborhoods.summary: The financial district: a dense wall of glass condo and office towers along Brickell Avenue and the bay, with rooftop bars and Brickell City Center.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown
neighborhoods.summary: Government buildings, the arena, Bayfront Park, museums on the bay and new towers, with MiamiCentral station for Brightline and Tri-Rail.

neighborhoods.name: Edgewater
neighborhoods.summary: Bayfront condo towers north of downtown around Margaret Pace Park, between Biscayne Boulevard and the water.

neighborhoods.name: Wynwood
neighborhoods.summary: Former warehouse district covered in murals, now galleries, breweries, cafes, bars and new mid-rise apartments.

neighborhoods.name: Midtown
neighborhoods.summary: A planned cluster of mid-rise apartments and big-box shops between Wynwood and the Design District.

neighborhoods.name: Design District
neighborhoods.summary: Luxury fashion boutiques, public art, galleries and chef-driven restaurants in a few walkable blocks.

neighborhoods.name: Little Haiti
neighborhoods.summary: The heart of Miami's Haitian community, with botanicas, Kreyol signage, a cultural complex and fast-rising rents.

neighborhoods.name: Little Havana
neighborhoods.summary: The historic center of Cuban exile Miami along Calle Ocho, with cafecito windows, domino games, cigar shops and live salsa.

neighborhoods.name: Overtown
neighborhoods.summary: Historic Black neighborhood once called the Harlem of the South, now mixing public housing, churches and new development near downtown.

neighborhoods.name: Allapattah
neighborhoods.summary: A working-class Dominican and Central American district of produce markets and garment shops, with new galleries arriving.

neighborhoods.name: Health District
neighborhoods.summary: The Civic Center medical campus around Jackson Memorial Hospital and the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, beside the courthouse buildings.

neighborhoods.name: Coconut Grove
neighborhoods.summary: Miami's oldest neighborhood: leafy, bayside and bohemian-turned-affluent, with marinas, sailing clubs and a walkable village center.

neighborhoods.name: Coral Gables
neighborhoods.summary: A planned 1920s Mediterranean Revival city of banyan-lined streets, the Biltmore, Miracle Mile and the University of Miami.

neighborhoods.name: Key Biscayne
neighborhoods.summary: A quiet island village across the Rickenbacker Causeway with beaches, parks and a lighthouse.

neighborhoods.name: South Beach
neighborhoods.summary: The southern end of Miami Beach: Art Deco hotels, Ocean Drive, Lincoln Road, nightlife and a wide sandy beach.

neighborhoods.name: Mid-Beach
neighborhoods.summary: Grand resort hotels like the Fontainebleau and Faena along Collins Avenue, with residential streets on Indian Creek behind them.

neighborhoods.name: North Beach
neighborhoods.summary: A calmer, more local stretch of Miami Beach with MiMo-style low-rise apartments, reaching up toward Surfside and Bal Harbor.

neighborhoods.name: Doral
neighborhoods.summary: A city west of the airport of warehouses, corporate headquarters, TV studios, golf and a large Venezuelan community.

neighborhoods.name: Kendall
neighborhoods.summary: Sprawling southwestern suburbs of strip malls, cul-de-sacs and Dadeland Mall, at the end of the Metrorail line.

neighborhoods.name: Westchester and University Park
neighborhoods.summary: Cuban-American suburban neighborhoods around Florida International University's main campus.

neighborhoods.name: Aventura
neighborhoods.summary: A northern condo city built around Aventura Mall, with a Brightline station.

neighborhoods.name: Miami Gardens
neighborhoods.summary: A largely Black, largely residential city in the north of the county, home to Hard Rock Stadium.

transit.name: Metrorail
transit.summary: Elevated heavy-rail lines from Dadeland through Coconut Grove, Brickell, downtown and the Health District to the airport and Hialeah.

transit.name: Metromover
transit.summary: A free automated people mover looping through downtown, Brickell and the Omni area.

transit.name: Metrobus
transit.summary: The county bus network, including routes across the causeways to Miami Beach and Key Biscayne.

transit.name: Free city trolleys
transit.summary: Free trolley-style bus routes run by the City of Miami, Coral Gables and Doral.

transit.name: Miami Beach Trolley
transit.summary: Free trolley loops through South Beach, Mid-Beach and North Beach.

transit.name: Brightline
transit.summary: Fast intercity trains from MiamiCentral via Aventura to Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach and Orlando.

transit.name: Tri-Rail
transit.summary: Regional commuter rail north to Broward and Palm Beach counties, serving the airport and MiamiCentral.

transit.name: Citi Bike Miami
transit.summary: Docked bike share in Miami and Miami Beach.

transit.name: Driving
transit.summary: Most of the metro is built around the car; expect heavy traffic on I-95, the Palmetto and the causeways.

annual_events.summary: Large outdoor juried art fair over Presidents' Day weekend.

annual_events.name: Calle Ocho Music Festival
annual_events.summary: A giant Latin street party on SW 8th Street, closing the Carnaval Miami season.

annual_events.name: Miami Music Week
annual_events.summary: A week of dance-music pool parties and club nights across Miami Beach and the mainland.

annual_events.name: Ultra Music Festival
annual_events.summary: Huge electronic music festival at Bayfront Park.

annual_events.name: Miami Open
annual_events.summary: Top-level tennis tournament held at Hard Rock Stadium.

annual_events.name: Miami Beach Pride
annual_events.summary: Parade and festival along Ocean Drive and Lummus Park.

annual_events.name: Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix
annual_events.summary: Race weekend on a circuit built around Hard Rock Stadium.

annual_events.name: Miami Spice
annual_events.summary: Restaurants across the county offer prix-fixe menus during the slow summer season.

annual_events.name: Dolphins football season
annual_events.summary: Sunday game days and tailgates at Hard Rock Stadium.

annual_events.name: Miami Book Fair
annual_events.summary: Week of author talks ending in a street fair at Miami Dade College's Wolfson Campus.

annual_events.name: Art Basel Miami Beach and Miami Art Week
annual_events.summary: The big art fair at the Miami Beach Convention Center, with satellite fairs and parties across the city.

annual_events.name: Orange Bowl
annual_events.summary: College football bowl game at Hard Rock Stadium around New Year.

local_color.name: Cafecito
local_color.summary: Cuban espresso brewed strong and whipped with sugar into a sweet foam (espumita), drunk in a few sips standing at a walk-up window.

local_color.name: Colada
local_color.summary: A larger cafecito in a styrofoam cup with a stack of thimble-sized plastic cups, bought to share around the office or job site.

local_color.name: Café con leche and tostada
local_color.summary: The Cuban breakfast: hot milk with espresso and pressed, buttered Cuban bread for dunking.

local_color.name: 3:05 cafecito
local_color.summary: Miami's area code is 305, so 3:05 in the afternoon has become a time for a coffee break, with people posting their cafecitos.

local_color.name: Ventanitas
local_color.summary: Walk-up coffee windows at Cuban restaurants and bakeries, where people stand for cafecito, pastelitos, croquetas and talk about politics.

local_color.name: Cuban sandwich
local_color.summary: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard pressed flat on Cuban bread; the medianoche is the same on a sweet egg roll.

local_color.name: Pastelitos and croquetas
local_color.summary: Flaky pastries filled with guava, guava and cream cheese, or meat, and fried ham croquetas, bought by the dozen for any gathering.

local_color.name: Frita
local_color.summary: The Cuban hamburger: a seasoned beef and chorizo patty with a pile of crisp shoestring potatoes on a soft bun.

local_color.name: Stone crab claws
local_color.summary: Florida stone crab claws are served cold and cracked with mustard sauce; the season opens in mid-October and runs into spring.

local_color.name: Pub sub
local_color.summary: Floridians are devoted to the made-to-order deli subs at Publix supermarkets, especially the chicken tender sub.

local_color.name: "Dale"
local_color.summary: All-purpose Miami Spanish for "go ahead", "let's go", "OK" or "bye", heard from everyone whatever their first language.

local_color.name: Miami Spanglish
local_color.summary: Conversations switch between English and Spanish mid-sentence, with phrases like "pero like" ("but, like") and greetings like the Cuban "¿qué bolá?" (what's up?).

local_color.name: Domino games
local_color.summary: Older men, many Cuban, play loud games of dominoes all day at the tables of Domino Park on Calle Ocho.

local_color.name: Hurricane prep
local_color.summary: From June through November people keep shutters, water, batteries and gas ready, and supermarket shelves empty fast when a storm is in the cone.

local_color.name: Miami Dolphins
local_color.summary: The NFL team plays at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, and fans never let anyone forget the 1972 perfect season.

local_color.name: Miami Heat
local_color.summary: The NBA team plays downtown at Kaseya Center and is known for "Heat Culture", its demanding work ethic, and for crowds dressed in all white for playoff games.

local_color.name: Miami Marlins
local_color.summary: The Major League Baseball team plays in Little Havana at loanDepot park, which has a retractable roof against summer rain.

local_color.name: Florida Panthers
local_color.summary: The NHL team plays in Sunrise, north of the city, and won back-to-back Stanley Cups in 2024 and 2025.

local_color.name: Inter Miami
local_color.summary: The MLS soccer club co-owned by David Beckham, which made Lionel Messi the city's most famous footballer when he signed in 2023.

local_color.name: Miami Hurricanes
local_color.summary: The University of Miami's teams, especially football, which plays at Hard Rock Stadium; fans flash the "U" with their hands.
